samples.summary: The corpus-version scoping check silently no-ops when the caller supplies no expected version, so labels about a different diff can enter the precision denominator
samples.evidence: `scoreValidity` guards the corpus scope with `if (corpusVersion !== null && l.corpus_version !== corpusVersion) refuse(...)`. When `corpusVersion` defaults to `null` (the library default on the exported entry point) the check is skipped entirely and labels from ANY corpus version are pooled into the same denominator — a judgement about different code counted as a judgement about this diff. This is the opposite fail direction the same file chose one check later for `parser_vintage`, where a missing current vintage is REFUSED (`status = "parse-vintage-unknown"`, `validity.mjs` joinLabels) with the comment "unknown is refused, not assumed current". A verification whose expected value never arrived should fail closed the same way in both places. Attack/abuse chain: any future caller (a report renderer, `score-all.mjs`) that omits `corpusVersion` gets a silently unscoped score with no state in the payload saying the check did not run — `completeness.verdict` still reads `complete`. The CLI happens to pass it, so this is not exploitable today.

samples.summary: The parser-vintage integrity check is skipped entirely for a label that simply omits the field, and `scoreValidity` never re-runs `validateLabel` to require it
samples.evidence: In `joinLabels`, both the `parse-vintage-unknown` and `stale-parse` branches are gated on `nonEmptyString(label.parser_vintage)`. A coderabbit label with `parser_vintage: null`/absent therefore skips the provenance check completely and falls through to `JOINED`, entering the precision denominator — exactly the state `labels.mjs:578` refuses because "a label with no parser vintage cannot be told from a current one". `scoreValidity`'s own validation loop checks `schema`, `arm`, `label_source` and `corpus_version` but never calls `validateLabel`, so the presence requirement is only enforced upstream in `adjudicate.mjs:605` (`readFindingLabels` → `validateLabel`). That makes the guard call-path-dependent: the CLI is covered, but `scoreValidity`/`joinLabels` are exported and any caller that assembles labels itself (or a future reader that skips `validateLabel`, as `readFindingLabels` itself once did per its own comment at adjudicate.mjs:577) gets stale-parse labels admitted as current with nothing in the join census saying so. Fail direction should be: no vintage on the coderabbit arm ⇒ not joined, not silently current.
searchedFor: Grep parser_vintage|parserVintage in scripts/agent/eval/labels.mjs (found the arm-conditional requirement at :578)
read validity.mjs joinLabels and scoreValidity validation loop in the diff

samples.summary: `--corpus-version` reaches a filesystem path in `readFindingLabels` unvalidated; the only thing preventing traversal outside the eval root is the order of two calls in the new CLI
samples.evidence: `readFindingLabels` builds `path.join(path.resolve(root), LABELS_DIR, corpusVersion, "findings")` with no segment validation, then `readdirSync`/`readFileSync` under it. The new CLI (`validity.mjs` main) passes `args["corpus-version"]` straight from argv. It is safe today only because `store.getCorpus(args["corpus-version"])` runs first and reaches `EvalStore._manifestPath` → `requireSegment` (`store.mjs:654`, grammar `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`), which rejects `..`, `/` and NUL. So the traversal guard for this new read path lives in an unrelated earlier call rather than at the read itself: reorder the two lines, or add a caller that reads labels without touching the manifest first, and `--corpus-version ../../../..` becomes a directory walk with `JSON.parse` of whatever is found (paths are then echoed to stderr and into the payload's `unreadable[]`). Hardening: validate the version as a path segment inside `readFindingLabels`, the way `store.mjs` does for every other segment.
searchedFor: checked call order in validity.mjs main(): getCorpus before readFindingLabels

samples.summary: The new CLI triggers GitHub API reads whose request path is interpolated from an unvalidated manifest field (`source_pr`), before the numeric validation runs
samples.evidence: `validity.mjs`'s CLI calls `corpusRecords(store, corpusVersion, …)`, which calls `fetchCodeRabbitPr(it.source_pr, …)`. There `n = String(pr ?? "").trim()` is interpolated straight into the request path: `api(["api", "--paginate", `repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/${n}/comments?per_page=100`])` (and `issues/${n}/comments`). The numeric guard `codeRabbitItemId` (`/^\d+$/`, coderabbit.mjs:322) only runs afterwards inside `codeRabbitRecords`, so a manifest whose `source_pr` is e.g. `1/comments?x=1&y=` or `../../../user` sends the ambient `gh` token to a different endpoint than intended and prints the response into the log — an API-path/SSRF-shaped injection bounded by whoever can write the eval-data manifest (a separate data repo, so not the reviewer's own PR). No shell is involved (`execFileSync("gh", args)`, gh-checks.mjs:27), so this is path manipulation only, not command injection. Pre-existing code; this change adds a second caller that reaches it.
searchedFor: Read gh-checks.mjs gh() to rule out shell:true
traced validity.mjs main() → corpusRecords call site

samples.summary: Absolute label file paths and raw finding summaries are echoed to stderr and into the `--json` payload with no redaction pass
samples.evidence: `console.error(`  ! unreadable label ${u.path}: ${u.reason}`)` prints absolute filesystem paths, `unreadable[]` carries them into the payload, `unmatched_keys`/`stale_parse_keys` carry `finding_key` (`file::summary`, i.e. verbatim reviewer text about the reviewed code), and `--json` dumps the whole payload to stdout. `scripts/agent/redact.mjs` exists and is used by the panel/hunt CLIs but not by any eval scorer, so this matches the local convention rather than breaking it — noted only because if this output is ever captured into a CI log or a PR comment it discloses local paths plus defect descriptions for the reviewed diffs. No credential material is printed; `parseArgs` uses a null-prototype accumulator (gh-checks.mjs:51), so `--__proto__ x` is not a pollution vector.
searchedFor: Grep redact across scripts/agent (22 files, none in eval/)
